dem_slope — DEM surface op

• Data kinds: depth → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.dem_slope(dem, cell_size, method='horn', units='degrees') (to call the implementation directly, import demops; demops.dem_slope(dem, cell_size, method='horn', units='degrees'); from the registry, opsdem.get("dem_slope"))

Usage

Slope angle. units is "degrees" / "radians" / "percent".

On a plane it agrees with the closed form atan(|grad|) (measured 1e-13 or less).

Procedure: from the 3x3 neighbourhood take dz/dx (eastward) and dz/dy (northward = direction of decreasing row), then g = hypot(dz/dx, dz/dy). "degrees" gives atan(g) in degrees, "radians" in radians, "percent" gives 100 g (45 degrees = 100 %). Edges are padded by replicating the border values (pad mode="edge"), so the outermost 1 cell comes out gentler than the interior.

• dem: (H, W) elevation [m], 3x3 or larger, real, no inf. Pass missing data as nan ―― if sentinel values like -9999 are left in (<= -9000 present and no nan), it is rejected. nan propagates over the 3x3 range.

• cell_size: cell edge length [m], positive finite. bool / strings rejected. For lat/lon grids use dem_geodetic_slope instead.

• method: "horn" (Horn 1981 3x3 weighted difference, default) / "central" (Zevenbergen–Thorne central difference).

• Return value: (H, W) float64. degrees is in [0, 90).

• All failures are ValueError (shape, sentinel values, cell_size, choices).

Used together with dem_aspect. dem_hillshade builds shading from these 2.
